## Summary

Did 2.4, the permission surface for unattended sessions. The problem it closes is that print mode has nobody to prompt: a gated tool call does not wait, it fails, so a driven session under the default mode cannot edit, test or commit and every session ends as a stall having done nothing. D8 settles the shape — the surface is a RUN property, its file a SESSION artifact. run_started gains an optional surface {permission_mode, allow, deny, model, effort}, omitted entirely when nothing was pinned because ambient is a different fact from unknown; --resume keeps the run's recorded surface over the new driver's flags and says so on the progress stream, exactly as it already does for threshold_pct, context_window and max_sessions. The file is written into each session's own temp dir beside the nudge, read back and compared before the spawn, and a mismatch throws instead of launching: verification is worth only its recency, and a file proven at run start says nothing about the session launched six sessions later. The /dev/null test proves the read-back catches a path that lies about storing what it was given. Mode rides --permission-mode because a flag cannot be outranked and a settings key can; rules ride the file. Default is acceptEdits plus the protocol floor and nothing else — mcp__sofar, Bash(sofar:*), and the LOCAL git verbs behind "commit code and record together" — with the project's own test and build commands left to --allow, since a table of likely test commands is one sofar could not keep true. No default deny: git push is simply absent from the allow-list so the mode gates it, and a default deny would be a trap under bypassPermissions. New module driver/permissions.ts, PermissionSurface deliberately identical in shape to the schema's RunSurface so nothing converts in either direction. Verified empirically against Claude Code 2.1.251 that mcp__<server> is a real server-level rule form and that --setting-sources must be left alone, since this repo's hooks live in project settings and its MCP server enablement in local settings. 1812 tests pass; an end-to-end run against a stub claude showed the flags on argv, the floor plus the operator's rule in the file, and the whole surface listed in sofar status.

## Next action

Phase 2 is complete, so start Phase 3, task 3.1: the second adapter that proves the contract. Read the surface it now has to render — LaunchRequest.surface is stated generically and each adapter turns it into its own config, so 3.1 is the first real test of whether that generic shape survives an agent that spells permissions differently. Note two things left open by 2.4: the per-session temp dir holding the nudge and settings file is never removed, which is arguably evidence worth keeping after an unattended run but is undocumented either way; and the surface is only ever proven at the FILE level, since proving the agent resolved it would cost a model call.
